deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 51–53 of cote 148). Grothendieck works with a groupoid, written S_*CD^±_top or S_*TD^±_top (the letter is hard to read). Its objects are triples (X, Σ, R):
- X is a compact oriented topological surface, with ± indicating orientation data.
- Σ is a closed 1-submanifold of 'cercles de découpage', i.e. a cut system or pants-type decomposition.
- R is a finite set of 'repères': marked points or markers on the boundary and cut circles.

On p. 51 he introduced 'graphes pendentifs à repères'. These are combinatorial graph data with a set of darts R⃗ carrying permutations σ0, σ1, which generate an action of the infinite dihedral group D_∞, the 'cartographic group'. He also gives canonical functors from S_*CD^±_top to (Gr.pend.rep) and to (Gr.bipend). He insists that any purely combinatorial model of the Teichmüller-type groupoid must recover these functors up to unique isomorphism. He then starts listing the 'opérations essentielles', which are the operations of the later Lego/Teichmüller tower. The first is (A1) 'gommage de repères': (X, Σ, R) together with R' ⊂ R goes to (X, Σ, R \ R').

This page (p. 9 of the sub-notes) is an NB on how to make this operation functorial.
- Suppose the groupoid S_*TD^±_top has been realised (reconstructed) by a groupoid of purely combinatorial descriptions, with its functor to (Gr.pend.rep).
- Then the data '(X, Σ, R) plus a subset R' ⊂ R' leads to a second groupoid S_*TD^±_top(R'), whose objects carry a marked subset R' of the repères.
- This groupoid has two functors to S_*TD^±_top:
  - the forgetful functor ('oubli des marquages R''), which keeps R but forgets which points are marked;
  - the erasure functor ('gommage de R''), which deletes the marked points.
- He asserts a commutative square: both composites to (Gr.pond), the weighted dual graphs of the decomposition, coincide.
- This holds only if the weighted graph does not record the repères. Hence the side remark: the target consists of graphs weighted by one invariant (probably the genus g) but not by the number of repères.
- The page ends 'alors qu'au niveau...'. The next page continues: '...des graphes pondérés à rubans', i.e. at the ribbon-graph level, gommage is reflected by deleting a D_∞-stable (σ0, σ1-stable) subset R⃗' ⊂ R⃗.
- Operation A2, erasing cut circles, then appears on p. 53 as contraction of edges, giving a 'generisation' morphism.

Purpose. This is part of the program, announced in Esquisse d'un programme, of describing the Teichmüller tower: the fundamental groupoids of moduli spaces M_{g,n} at base points of maximal degeneration. The description should be by generators and relations, and should be functorial with respect to the elementary operations: forgetting points and cutting or gluing along circles. Here the topological counterpart of the forgetful maps M_{g,n+m} → M_{g,n} is being lifted to the combinatorial (ribbon/dart) models.

The long diagonal marginal NB is largely illegible. It appears to comment on what this operation looks like in Teichmüller terms, with a mention of Σ^+ and groups.
errors: Possible gap: erasing repères can make a piece of the decomposition unstable. Examples are a disc or an annulus component, or a sphere with fewer than 3 special points after removing marked points. In the algebraic setting this requires Knudsen-type contraction/stabilization, and in the topological cut-system setting it requires removing superfluous cut circles. The page does not address whether the result of gommage is still an object of the groupoid, or whether a stabilization step is needed. It may be implicit in his definitions on earlier pages, where repères might lie only on cut circles and not count toward stability.

The commutativity of the square to (Gr.pond) is only valid if the weighting ignores the repères. Grothendieck seems to note this himself in the bottom-right remark ('graphes ... pondérés par g, mais non par r' – reading uncertain), so this is a qualification rather than an error.
Nothing is verified on the page; it states only the existence of the functors and the commutative diagram.

ideas.what: Groupoid of surfaces with cut systems and marked points, (X, Σ, R), modelled by purely combinatorial data (pendant graphs with repères, darts with σ0, σ1 / D_∞ action), with canonical functors to graph categories
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial (ribbon-graph / cut-system / pants-decomposition) models of the Teichmüller groupoid or mapping-class-group groupoid; Lego–Teichmüller game
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984); Hatcher–Thurston 1980 and Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps 2000 for pants complexes; Bakalov–Kirillov; Moore–Seiberg
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §§2–3 on the Teichmüller tower and Lego game (in outline only; not this formalism)

ideas.what: 'Gommage de repères': erasing a subset R' of marked points as a functor S_*TD(R') → S_*TD, together with the forgetful functor, in a commutative diagram over weighted dual graphs
ideas.modern_name: Forgetful (point-erasing) maps M_{g,n+m} → M_{g,n} at the level of Teichmüller groupoids / mapping class groups (Birman exact sequence); compatibility with stratification by dual graphs
ideas.usually_credited_to: Knudsen (1983) for stable curves; Birman (1969) for mapping class groups; Ihara/Nakamura/Schneps et al. for the Teichmüller tower
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions the tower being stable under erasing points and cutting, without this functorial diagram

ideas.what: At the ribbon/dart level, erasing repères corresponds to deleting a D_∞-stable subset of darts
ideas.modern_name: Forgetful operation on ribbon graphs / dessins (combinatorial forgetful map)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Penner and Kontsevich, implicitly, in ribbon-graph decompositions of moduli space (where forgetful maps are known to be non-cellular)

missed.claim: Grothendieck wants the purely combinatorial model of the Teichmüller groupoid to be functorial for erasing marked points: a functor between groupoids of marked/unmarked combinatorial objects lifting the forgetful maps. He wants it compatible with the map to weighted dual graphs and realised on darts by deleting a D_∞-stable subset. It is not completed here (the stability issue is not treated). The later literature on combinatorial models handles forgetful maps awkwardly (e.g. via the Birman sequence); this program of lifting them to dart/ribbon data is not, to my knowledge, worked out in this form.
missed.quote: S_*TD^±_top(…R'…) --gommage de R'--> S_*TD^±_top ; ↓ oubli des marquages R' ; … (Gr. pond)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Functoriality of combinatorial models under forgetful maps is relevant to the Grothendieck–Teichmüller action on the tower (compatibility with point-erasing is one of the defining constraints of GT-type groups). It also bears on the operadic/modular-operad structure of moduli spaces. The idea is mostly standard in spirit, however.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a programmatic page setting up a standard operation (forgetting marked points) as a functor with a commutative diagram, within the known Teichmüller-tower/Lego program of the Esquisse. The ribbon-level (D_∞-stable darts) formulation is a nice unpublished detail but not a substantial new result.
transcription_corrections: The groupoid symbol is written S_*CD^±_top (as on p. 51) or S_*TD^±_top; the letter after S is ambiguous, plausibly a script C/T.
The target of the first functor reads '(Gr. pend. rep)' (graphes pendentifs à repères), not '(Gr. fond. rep)'.
The bottom target of the commutative diagram reads '(Gr. pond)' (graphes pondérés), not '(Gr. fond)'.

The right-hand note likely reads 'graphes pondérés par g, mais non par r' (weighted by genus but not by number of repères) rather than 'graphes non pondérés par σ, mais ...'; the reading is uncertain.
The words above the gommage arrow read 'gommage de R'' and below the vertical arrow 'oubli des marquages R''.
The top line probably reads 'Ayant ainsi un groupoïde équivalent (de descriptions purement combinatoires) "reconstruisant" [réalisant] le groupoïde ...'.
